review: RMSNorm reduces the last normalized dimensions, uses explicit epsilon, and multiplies by weights after normalization.
PyTorch 2.8.0 uses Float32 opmath for Float32 inputs; half and bfloat16 are upcast, outside this prototype.
CPU rms_norm is composed from tensor arithmetic in this version; Inductor compilation is included as a stronger baseline.
The fused residual operation is a standard composition, independently implemented with two Julia passes; no upstream implementation is copied.

The embedded runtime initializes once; callback pointers are obtained at runtime, Julia exceptions stay inside the ABI, host buffer lifetimes remain with the synchronous caller, and calls stay on the initializing thread.

The CPU index reported stable torch 2.14.1+cpu. In this version rms_norm_symint dispatches to _fused_rms_norm, so 2.8 performance cannot establish a current-framework advantage. Current pinned requirements and additional trials use 2.14.1; old receipts and a small separate 2.8 hash lock are retained.
